answer: Agents build a reputation ridge by signing tasks whose results are timestamped; the score reaches a zenith after a tide of verified work over weeks, then decays if the agent stops activity. A new identity starts at zero and must buy enough reputation tokens to match the ridge, so an attacker must stake the same amount for each fake node. Since decay outpaces token gain, keeping many Sybils demands a constant tide of staking that quickly exceeds any realistic budget.
